O*NET 19-4012.00 agricultural technicians: work with agricultural scientists on plant, fibre and animal research, or assist with animal breeding and nutrition; set up or maintain laboratory equipment, collect samples from crops or animals, prepare specimens and record data, and raise crop yields and quality or strengthen plant and animal resistance to pests and diseases through tests and experiments. Core tasks include land preparation and tillage, operating agricultural machinery, recording experimental and research data, maintaining and repairing agricultural facilities and equipment, collecting and inspecting plant and animal samples, setting up laboratory or field equipment for on-site testing, and supervising and training other technicians and agricultural workers. This profile is a U.S. single-occupation basis.

entries: Field and facility work｜Land preparation, tillage and machinery｜Prepare land, till, weed, prune and harvest to the plan, operate machinery such as tractors and sprayers, and follow the safety procedures.

Equipment preparation and maintenance｜Inspection and repair｜Set up laboratory or field equipment for the testing needed, maintain and repair agricultural facilities, equipment and tools, and keep them running and clean.
Sampling｜Collecting and labelling samples｜Collect samples from crops or animals, label them by object, time and location, and record the sampling conditions and storage requirements.

Preparation and testing｜Processing and measuring to protocol｜Prepare laboratory samples, weigh reagents and prepare culture media to the standard protocol, and complete tests with a spectrometer, centrifuge or pH meter.
Data and records｜Recording and organising｜Record experimental, research and animal-husbandry data faithfully, and organise data summaries and reports with units, charts and notes on anomalies.

Collaboration and supervision｜Training and coordination｜Work with researchers to advance the plan, supervise or train other technicians and agricultural workers, and report progress and anomalies as required.

values: AT26-V1: complete fictional input

All paper. Date 2026-10-01; the fictional plan AT26-V1 specifies three points P1/P2/P3, each with one independent sample bag of 120g, numbered AT26-S1/S2/S3 and not mixed; the planned collection is 10:00, and the storage condition is the task-statement label 'SIM storage', which does not represent a real sample condition. On receipt S1/P1 11:00 had an intact seal, S2/P2 11:10 a broken seal and S3/P3 11:20 an intact seal, all recorded at 120g.

Simulated ledger: balance B01 valid until 2026-10-03; pH device M01 valid until 2026-09-30. Three records (tare g/gross g/simulated volume mL/raw pH): S1 20.0/25.0/25/6.2; S2 22.0/27.0/25/6.8; S3 21.0/25.5/25/missing. Net weight = gross weight − tare weight; the stated weight range is 4.9—5.1g inclusive. No solution is actually prepared, no pH is measured and no sampling is done.

Stated status rules: any one of a broken seal, a weight outside the range, an expired device or a missing pH marks the item 'to be confirmed'; the simulated readings may be recorded, but a reading from an expired device must not be treated as a valid result. All raw values are kept, with no repeat measurement and no change of value; device and sample corrections are confirmed by the simulated supervisor, and this exercise provides no follow-up result.
Tasks and reference deliverable

Task: write the three-record ledger of number — point — time — storage — seal; calculate the net weights and check the weights; check the validity of the two devices; list each anomaly and item to be confirmed; and answer whether a valid mean pH can be calculated or a quality conclusion drawn. Use only the input of this task and do not look for an external plan.

Reference: S1/P1/10:00→11:00/SIM storage/intact, S2/P2/10:00→11:10/SIM storage/broken, S3/P3/10:00→11:20/SIM storage/intact; net weights 5.0/5.0/4.5g, with S3 below 4.9g. Comparison feedback and the fixed scale

8 points, 1 each: all three net weights correct; the S3 weight outside the range identified; the S2 seal broken; M01 expired; the S3 pH missing; raw values not altered or filled in; all three to be confirmed; no valid mean or quality conclusion. Candidate A delivers 'net weights 5/5/5; all seals intact; M01 valid; S3 filled in as 6.5; all three acceptable, mean pH 6.5' and scores 0/8; the feedback checks each item against the raw input and withdraws the changed value and the conclusion.
